Bug_Title: Set appropriate Status Codes on HTTP responses
Bug_Details:
The request handler function in a Controller should set the appropriate HTTP status code based on the operation’s success or failure.
This is done by returning a Response object with the appropriate status code.
If an exception is thrown during the execution of the handler, the status code should be in the range of 4xx or 5xx. Examples of such codes are BAD_REQUEST , UNAUTHORIZED , FORBIDDEN , NOT_FOUND , INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR , BAD_GATEWAY , SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE , etc.
The status code should be 1xx, 2xx, or 3xx if no exception is thrown and the operation is considered successful. Such codes include OK , CREATED , MOVED_PERMANENTLY , FOUND , etc.
Bug_Explanation: The method'showBug' is using HttpServletResponse constants to set the status code of the HTTP response. But the HttpServletResponse class is not imported in this file. Instead, a lambda function is used to set the status code.
Trigger_Explanation: The method showBug in class BugExample doesn't return any status code. The status codes are hard coded in the getStatusCode method. The test shows how these hard coded values are used.
Model_Explanation: The code does not contain a bug as described in the bug description. The function showBug(boolean isSuccess) returns the status code based on the input parameter isSuccess. If isSuccess is true, it returns 200 (HTTP OK status code), otherwise it returns 400 (HTTP Bad Request status code). This is consistent with the bug description, where the function should return the appropriate HTTP status code based on the operation’s success or failure.
